The reference EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1195-1320) applies the identical thresholds to Nj, the neighbor count of the ONE atom being processed: 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', '(nl23>0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl33>0) && (Nj>3)', '(nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2)', '(nl34>0) && (Nj>4)', '(nl44>0) && (Nj>5)', and this is the routine PairPOD::compute() actually calls (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:214).  Consequence: for an atom with <=5 neighbors sitting in a block that has many pairs overall, KOKKOS evaluates three-/four-body and cross descriptors that the CPU sets to zero (bd1 is zeroed first, eapod.cpp:1207), and those descriptors are not zero for small Nj (e.g. d33 = d3*d3 from a single-neighbor sumU).
